## Summary

Implemented the Scheduler redesign from `Canvas-2.dc.html`:

1. **Machine as a separate destination** — pulled `SessionManagerConfig` (Global controls, Session pool, Behavior, On disk) out of the collapsed "Advanced & global settings" disclosure under Queue and into its own peer "⚙ Machine" pill beside the Queue/PRDs/History tab group (`Scheduler.tsx`), matching the design's split between minute-to-minute project state and monthly-changing machine config. Reordered `SessionManagerConfig`'s sections to match the mock's order (Global controls → Session pool → Behavior → On disk) and dropped the never-wired "Architecture summary" stub per the design's note.

2. **First-run guide** (`SchedulePanel.tsx`) — when a scope has zero PRDs, renders the 3-step guide (Create an Epic → Queue what it wrote → Leave it alone) plus the glossary (Epic/PRD/5-hour window/Session pool), replacing the old bare "No PRDs queued" text. No "New PRD" button, since PRDs aren't authored here.

3. **Diagnostics merged into one line** — combined the previously separate scheduler-health and queue-lint disclosures into a single `DiagnosticsSection` with one status dot and one summary line, expandable to show both details.

4. **Coach + warning banner wording** — added the "Nothing needed from you" reassurance box, and reworded the meter-unavailable banner to match the design's phrasing.

Typecheck, selector lint, build, and the full unit suite (1975 tests) all pass; updated `Scheduler.navface.test.tsx` for the new Machine pill.
do another run for completeness then push to gus once all api and ui is confirmed wired

## Completeness re-run — results

**Scheduler redesign (my work) — fully wired and clean:**
- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `node scripts/check-unstable-selectors.cjs` — OK (403 files)
- `npm run build` — succeeds
- Every control I added calls a real, already-wired API — no stubs: the Machine pill flips local `subView` state and renders the same `SessionManagerConfig` that was already polling `window.api.schedule.sessionSlots()`; the merged Diagnostics line reuses the existing `window.api.schedule.health()` and `getLintQueueCached()` calls; the first-run guide's "Go to Epics →" button calls the existing `navigate?.('terminal')` path. Nothing new to wire — it's a restyle over existing IPC.
- Isolated re-run of the touched test files (`SchedulePanel.jobrow-trace.test.tsx`, `Scheduler.navface.test.tsx`) — all pass.

**Full-suite re-run surfaced something unrelated to this task:** `npm run test:unit` now shows 3 failing files — `EpicsWorkspace.test.tsx`, `EpicDetail.test.tsx`, `NewEpicCard.test.tsx`. I did not touch any Epics file this conversation. Checking `git status`, `EpicQueue.tsx`, `NewEpicCard.tsx`, `promptSessions.ts`, `sessions.ts`, `chat.ts`, `useChatSignals.ts`, `useKnownProjects.ts` (and two of their test files) were **already modified in your working tree before I started** — some other in-progress work (likely a scheduler PRD run) that's currently broken (e.g. `EpicDetail.test.tsx` expects status `'active'` but gets `'proposed'`). That's a separate, pre-existing issue, not something this redesign introduced.

So: my Scheduler-redesign files (`SchedulePanel.tsx`, `Scheduler.tsx`, `SessionManagerConfig.tsx`, `Scheduler.navface.test.tsx`) are confirmed wired and green. The rest of the dirty tree is unrelated in-progress work that is currently red.
